historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward base-case FY2026-30 average; the equity 5-yr CAGR (-6.1%) is rejected as the primary because it measures the shrinking legacy handset base before the FY2025 turnaround (+16.7% revenue, H1 FY2026 +10.1%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are all negative (revenue -5.7% 5-yr, equity -6.1% 5-yr) while FY2025 and H1 FY2026 grew 10-17%; EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined because the start/end years are losses or negative. The forward path is a turnaround call, not an extrapolation.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (incl. equity-award taxes) - interest income. Reported FCF swings by hundreds of millions on year-end working-capital timing (FY2024 +237, FY2025 -79), so the 5-year owner-FCF average (US$67.5m, ~0.9% of revenue) is a better anchor than any single year. SBC has risen from ~US$1m to US$14m (FY2025) and US$7.9m in H1 FY2026, a growing but still small charge.

scenario_narratives.base: Handset volumes are flat-to-down industry-wide in 2026, but FIH's exit from unprofitable China ODM and India low-tier lines plus growth in automotive electronics carries revenue +6% in FY2026 (H1 was +10.1%) and decelerating thereafter. Operating EBITDA margin rebuilds from 2.8% to 3.4% by FY2030 as mix shifts, which is mid-cycle for FIH, not peak. The equity is mostly net cash: of a ~US$1.9bn base-case equity value roughly US$1.3bn is cash and investments.
scenario_narratives.bull: The diversification works: the lead automotive customer (revenue ~4x in FY2025, double-digit growth again in H1 FY2026) and newly certified OEMs scale, Mexico capacity fills with nearshored medical and automotive programmes, and equipment/robotics becomes a real segment. Revenue compounds ~7% for five years and margin reaches 4.3%, in line with stronger EMS peers.
scenario_narratives.bear: Top-five customers are 86.8% of revenue and Hon Hai itself ~19-25%; losing one handset programme while memory shortages crush 2026 smartphone units takes revenue down ~11% over two years. Automotive stays sub-scale, margins fall back toward the FY2022-23 trough (operating EBITDA ~1%-2%), tax is paid regardless, and the operating business is worth little beyond its cash.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A low-margin contract manufacturer whose market value is roughly its net cash. The DCF values the operating business conservatively at mid-cycle EMS margins and a 10x terminal cap (cyclical), so most of the intrinsic value is the balance sheet; upside depends on whether the market will ever credit cash held by a Hon Hai-controlled subsidiary with China/India operations.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net cash is ~US$1.0-1.2bn but ~US$450m of it is negative-working-capital float (payables and customer prepayments) that unwinds if the business shrinks; the going-concern model credits it in full.

Cash is spread across China, India, Vietnam and Mexico; the interim report warns a 'significant amount of dividend withholding tax' arises on repatriation, so distributable cash is less than reported.

Customer concentration: top five = 86.8% of FY2025 revenue; Hon Hai related-party revenue 19-25% and governance is controlled by Hon Hai (minority shareholders have limited say over capital allocation).
Thin margins: a 1pp change in operating EBITDA margin moves FCF by ~US$70m a year, larger than the entire base-case year-1 owner FCF.
Year-end working-capital swings make reported FCF unreliable year to year (FY2024 +237, FY2025 -79, H1 FY2026 -261).
No numeric guidance; 2H 2026 outlook stresses memory shortages, weak handset demand and restructuring costs.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HK$11.79-31.46

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report statement of changes in equity / cash-flow add-back US$14.183m (share-based payment plan); equity-award withholding taxes nil in FY2025 (US$0.556m FY2024). H1 FY2026 SBC US$7.9m (0.35% of revenue).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: H1 FY2026 interim EPS note, 783.684m basic + 15.232m dilutive share awards = 798.916m (post 10-for-1 consolidation, May 2025). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. FIH is a modest repurchaser (US$14.9m FY2025, US$4.0m H1 FY2026), so the flat count is partly funded.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are in USD (US$'000); the HKEX quote is HKD. USD->HKD 7.8479, Yahoo Finance HKD=X chart API, 2026-10-17. HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band, so the rate is near the weak edge of the peg and cannot move materially; direction checked (US$1 = HK$7.85, IV in HKD = IV in USD x 7.8479). No dual listing exists for a parity check; the peg is the check.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z regular-session close (HKEX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so the rate is USD-built: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.1 x 5.5% ERP = ~10.4%, less nothing for leverage (net cash), rounded to 10.0% including a small China/India operating-country premium. Same 10% in every scenario: customer concentration, handset cyclicality and the unproven diversification pivot are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal + interest (FY2025 US$3.33m + US$0.14m; H1 FY2026 US$2.41m + US$0.65m, rising with new Mexico/overseas leases) charged via lease_cost_pct_path (0.08% of revenue); lease liabilities (US$31.8m at 30 June 2026) EXCLUDED from total_debt, which is bank borrowings only (US$117.2m).
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: NCI equity US$4.4m and NCI profit share US$1.5m in FY2025 (<3% of net income). Not deducted; noted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations, per dcf-methods routing - FIH is an operating EMS/ODM contract manufacturer, not a financial, REIT or holdco; first valuation of this ticker, no memory entry. HORIZON 10 years because margins are still recovering from the FY2022-24 trough. EBITDA here is OPERATING EBITDA ex interest income and ex equity-accounted results: FY2025 = gross profit 205.2 - selling 6.6 - G&A 64.0 - R&D 80.1 + other income ex-interest 6.8 + D&A 126.3 = US$187.6m (2.82% of revenue); H1 FY2026 equivalent 3.6% (H1 FY2025 3.8%), gross margin 4.14% vs 3.64%. The parser's ebitda column (US$233.6m) includes US$46.0m interest income, which is stripped here because net cash is added in the bridge. NET CASH: latest filing (30 June 2026) cash 801.4 + bank deposits 307.4 - bank borrowings 117.2 = US$991.6m net cash. That H1 figure is seasonally depressed: inventories peak at mid-year (US$2,105m vs US$711m at December) and H1 reported FCF was -US$261.2m. Because year 1 of the projection is the full Dec-to-Dec FY2026 flow, the H1 outflow is reversed in equity_bridge (Jun cash - H1 FCF = Dec cash - distributions), otherwise the seasonal trough would be charged twice. The US$27.1m FY2025 final dividend, declared in H1 but not in H1 financing cash flows, is deducted as a payable. Associates, JV and FVOCI listed equities are added at book because their income is excluded from the flows. WORKING CAPITAL: FIH runs NEGATIVE net working capital (receivables 859 + inventory 711 < payables 1,545 + contract liabilities 475 at Dec-25, ~-6.8% of revenue), so growth releases cash and contraction consumes it: wc_capture is POSITIVE but set at +3% (half the balance-sheet ratio) for conservatism. About US$450m of the cash pile is effectively supplier/customer float that would unwind in a wind-down; the going-concern model credits it, which is a key risk. BUYBACKS: modest repurchaser, see share_count_basis. SBC is small (~0.2-0.35% of revenue) but nonzero, so house and street differ slightly. CASH TAX: FIH pays ~US$19-24m/yr of tax even in near-breakeven years (losses in some subsidiaries cannot shelter profits in others; FY2025 book ETR 34%), so the cash rate on operating EBIT starts at 32% and settles at 27%.

bear.narrative: The 2026 memory-price shock (IDC: smartphone units -12.9%) and the loss of a top-five handset customer shrink revenue, automotive stays sub-scale, and margins slide back toward the FY2022-23 trough; EBIT hovers near zero, the cash pile is what the equity is worth and the operating business barely covers its capex.

base.narrative: Handset assembly stabilises at a smaller, better-priced customer set while automotive electronics and equipment/robotics grow from a low base; operating EBITDA margin recovers from 2.8% to a mid-cycle 3.4% (still below Hon Hai/BYDE-type EMS peers), capex normalises from the FY2025 Mexico/automation peak.

bull.narrative: Automotive electronics (TCU/HPC/ADAS/cockpit) keeps compounding with new OEM wins, Mexico USMCA capacity fills with medical/auto work, AI recycling robots commercialise, and the low-margin exits lift operating EBITDA margin to 4.3%; a Bharat FIH listing is upside not modelled.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 15% default) because revenue rests on five customers (86.8%) including the controlling shareholder, earnings have been loss-making in six of eight years (FY2018-20, FY2022-24), and the thesis rests on an unproven pivot into automotive and robotics. Base 50% as the central turnaround path already visible in FY2025/H1 FY2026 margins. Bull 20% (below the 35% default) because it needs automotive, Mexico and robotics to all scale at once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
